🐉🇲🇽 How the Belt & Road enters Mexico: through Michoacán's governor

China's ambassador Chen Daojiang met Governor Alfredo Ramírez Bedolla on June 5 to "materialize cooperation" at Lázaro Cárdenas — Mexico's second-largest port and the country's main maritime gateway for trade with China. The plan: expand port capacity and commercialize Michoacán's designation-of-origin products into Chinese markets.

Bedolla also announced that in July 2026, Morelia will open bidding to acquire Chinese-made hybrid buses for the Morebús transit system. Concrete BRI infrastructure entering Mexico not through CDMX but through subnational diplomacy — exactly the channel Washington has no leverage to close.

While the US screams about Chinese investment, Mexican governors are signing memorandums. Mexico is diversifying one port, one bus fleet at a time.

🇲🇽🔥 Trump says "not renewing." Ebrard signs joint statements.

The second round of USMCA review talks closed June 17 in Washington. The official joint statement from Greer and Ebrard, released June 18, lists what they actually did: advanced rules of origin for industrial goods, opened conceptual discussions on agriculture, labor, environment, and established a new committee to oversee Chapter 12 sectoral annexes.

Round 3 is already scheduled for Mexico City next month. Trump can post "not looking to renew" all he wants — Mexico's economy ministry is the one writing the structures that will outlive him. The 50% Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum remain the open wound: Mexico calls them "unsustainable," and US negotiators concede 350,000 auto jobs are at risk.

Sovereignty is showing up to every round, building committees, and outwaiting the tantrum.

🇲🇽🎨 500 actions. 200,000 new upper-secondary spaces. "Expanding secondaries so their evening shift becomes a preparatoria. Expanding existing preparatorias. New preparatorias. And the new model that begins this year: Bachillerato Nacional 'Margarita Maza.'" — Claudia Sheinbaum, CBTis No. 290 inauguration, Tijuana Saturday's event opened a tech bachillerato carrying an Artificial Intelligence track. One student, Melina, said her commute is 10 minutes — "the only prepa that has this Intelligence."

🇲🇽🎨 "Education is a right, not a privilege." "We're going to keep building more preparatorias close to home." — Claudia Sheinbaum, inaugurating CBTis No. 290, Tijuana The new tech high school sits in what the governor called "a historically forgotten, lagging zone" of Tijuana. Part of 500 education actions in 2025-26 adding 200,000 new upper-secondary spaces under the Bachillerato Nacional "Margarita Maza."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICAN ECONOMY FROZE IN MAY — INEGI IOAE 0.0% MONTHLY, INDUSTRY CONTRACTS 0.2%</u>

INEGI's Timely Economic Activity Indicator (IOAE) registered 0.0% monthly change in May, with annual growth decelerating to 1.0–1.1% from 1.4% in April. Secondary activities (manufacturing, construction, mining) contracted 0.2% monthly and grew only 0.7% annually — the weakest flank. Tertiary (commerce and services) held at 1.7% annual. The IGAE level sat unchanged at 106.3 points between April and May. Trump's tariff war and T-MEC uncertainty starting to bite the real economy where manufacturing meets the border.

Source: El Economista / INEGI

🇲🇽🌎 <u>CDMX SECURES FREE WORLD CUP ACCESS — 130 MDP PRIVATE + 23 BILLION PESOS IN PUBLIC INFRA</u>

Mexico City Head of Government Clara Brugada locked in agreements worth 130–135 million pesos with 30+ private companies including Visa México to broadcast every World Cup match free across 18 public sites — layered atop 23 billion pesos in public infrastructure upgrades to light rail and BRT. The Zócalo Fan Fest has already exceeded 500,000 attendees. Officials called it "una fiesta intercultural sin precedentes." Total event organization budget: 180 million pesos. Public access to global sport, financed without gouging the public.

Source: Regeneración

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHCP DOCUMENTS 4.3 BILLION PESO TAX EVASION BY JUEGOS DEL BAJÍO — PERMITS FROM FOX/CREEL ERA</u>

Mexico's Treasury Ministry has formally documented 4,306,799,683 pesos in taxes evaded by casino company Juegos del Bajío, owned by the Rodríguez Borgio brothers and originally licensed under Vicente Fox with Santiago Creel as Interior Secretary. The evasion ran through a fabricated 2019 notarized loan contract — the notary supposedly involved told SHCP in January 2024 he never processed the document. SCJN reviews the case June 4; Justice Lenia Batres is pushing acceptance, Yasmín Esquivel opposes. The old PAN-era corporate-state pipeline still getting unwound.

Source: Contralínea

🇲🇽🏭 <u>SHEINBAUM CALLS FOR NATIONAL DEBATE ON AI AND DIGITAL PLATFORMS</u>

"No podemos ser omisos y decir 'no pasa nada'" — President Sheinbaum opened the door to regulating AI, deepfakes manipulating politicians' voices and images, screen addiction among youth, AI-driven homework dependence, and — the real target — private corporate control over platform algorithms. Several Mexican states already ban cellphones in elementary schools. The debate widens to platform usage duration, electoral campaign AI, and ethical governance of foreign-owned algorithms. Mexico drawing the digital sovereignty line.

Source: Contralínea

🇲🇽🌎 <u>CANADA HITS CANNED VEGETABLES WITH 10% TARIFF — MEXICO EXEMPTED UNDER T-MEC</u>

Canada imposed a 10% tariff on canned vegetable imports Friday, valid up to 200 days. Mexico, the United States, Israel, Chile and developing countries were all exempted — Ottawa cited its existing trade obligations under T-MEC. The Canadian International Trade Tribunal will rule by September 9 on whether domestic producers were actually harmed; if not, the tariff is suspended. Treaty discipline still functioning on the northern border while Washington fires tariffs at the rest of the world.

Source: La Jornada

🚨🇲🇽 <u>HACIENDA CUTS FUEL SUBSIDIES — PREMIUM PAYS FULL IEPS, MAGNA 9.89%, DIESEL 20.89%</u>

Mexico's Treasury Ministry just slashed fuel subsidies for June 20–26 as international oil prices drop. The federation now covers only 20.89% of IEPS on diesel (consumers pay 5.82 pesos/liter), 9.89% on Magna (6.03 pesos/liter), and ZERO on Premium — the full 5.65 pesos per liter passes through. Mexico letting markets clear while keeping the caps that actually matter.

Source: La Jornada
